findings.issue: Game selection is read only from useSearchParams() and written with native window.history.replaceState; Next has open issues and 16.4-specific reports where replaceState does not re-sync useSearchParams, so the URL would show the new game while the select and tables snap back to the old one.
findings.suggestion: Keep the selected game in component state seeded from the server-rendered searchParams prop, sync it on popstate, and write the URL from that state (or use router.replace so the router owns the change).

findings.issue: getMoves fetches the full record of every move the Pokémon knows in any game (e.g. ~250 for Mew) even though only one version group's moves are displayed.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the requested game from searchParams first (it's available server-side), then fetch move records only for that game's learns.

findings.issue: decodeURIComponent(name) throws a URIError for malformed input like /pokemon/%zz, producing a 500 instead of the spec's Not found page (same pattern in moves, abilities and types pages).
findings.suggestion: Wrap the decode in try/catch and fall through to notFound(), or validate the name before decoding.

findings.issue: A hand-rolled TTL/promise Map cache re-implements what fetch's Data Cache (`next: { revalidate: 30 }`) provides, adding bespoke cache code a team must maintain.
findings.suggestion: Either switch to `fetch(url, { next: { revalidate: 30 } })` (dynamic rendering via connection() still guarantees no build-time fetching), or keep the cache but document why the framework cache was rejected.

findings.issue: Pagination uses preventDefault-ed <a> + window.history.pushState; entries created outside the router make back/forward a full page reload, and manual scrollTo replaces Link's default behavior.
findings.suggestion: Use <Link href> or router.push for pagination (entries are already client-side, so navigation stays cheap), or document the shallow-routing tradeoff at the call site.

findings.issue: No error.tsx or loading.tsx anywhere: an API failure renders Next's default error page and Pokémon pages (which await dozens of upstream fetches) show nothing until they resolve.
findings.suggestion: Add a root error boundary and a loading.tsx for /pokemon/[name] (and the list pages) so failures and slow responses look intentional.

findings.issue: API payloads are handled as `any` throughout (also abilities/[name]/page.tsx:27, types/[name]/page.tsx:65), so typos on field names won't be caught and readers must consult the API to know shapes.
findings.suggestion: Define minimal interfaces for the resources the app touches (species, pokemon, move, ability, type, version-group) and type api<T> at the call sites.

findings.issue: IndexEntry is a positional tuple ([id, name, types, generation]) consumed as e[1]/e[2]/e[3] in both page.tsx and HomeView, hurting readability and refactor safety.
findings.suggestion: Use a named-field object type for the serialized index entries.

findings.issue: An out-of-range ?page= value is clamped for display but left in the URL, so 'Page x of y' and the URL disagree after load.
findings.suggestion: When filters.page exceeds pageCount, replaceState to the clamped URL (or render the clamped number into the pagination links consistently).

summary: A clean, current-generation App Router codebase: dynamic rendering via connection(), async params, metadata/viewport exports, notFound-based 404s and small well-bounded lib/components with good why-comments. The main risks are client URL state managed with native history.replaceState where the hook's re-sync is not guaranteed on Next 16.4, plus a per-page fan-out that fetches every move record regardless of the selected game. I'd merge after one focused round fixing the game-select sync, the fan-out, and the malformed-name 500.
